example: The review offered a nuanced account of the character's loyalty and resentment.
nuance: Nuanced concerns meaningful distinctions, not vagueness or unnecessary complexity.
prompt: A critique distinguishes several shades of meaning instead of making a blanket judgment.
options: Her nuanced critique separated the policy's intentions from its uneven results.
His nuanced verdict declared every aspect either perfect or worthless.
The nuanced report used complicated words but ignored all distinctions.
Her nuanced critique stayed so vague that no reader could tell what she actually thought.
reasons: This sentence demonstrates the meaning: showing or recognizing subtle distinctions.
A rigid either-or verdict suppresses subtle distinctions.
Complex language does not by itself demonstrate subtle understanding.
Vagueness hides judgments, while nuance makes fine distinctions clear and specific.

practice.prompt: A piano teacher gives a student feedback right after a recital.
options: His nuanced feedback summed up the entire recital with one word: good.
The student's nuanced habit of tapping her foot loudly distracted the audience.
The feedback counted as nuanced simply because it repeated the same compliment across three full pages.
Her nuanced feedback praised the steady rhythm but noted that the soft passages felt rushed.
reasons: A one-word verdict on the whole performance makes no distinctions at all.
This confuses the word with nuisance; an annoying habit has nothing to do with subtlety.
Length isn't subtlety; repeating one point over and over draws no fine distinctions.
Telling apart what went well from what needs work shows careful attention to fine differences.
